{"code": "import pandas as pd

df = pd.read_csv('data/trial.csv')

# Deduplicate by patient_id, keeping the row with the highest sample_seq
df = df.sort_values('patient_id').sort_values('sample_seq', ascending=False).drop_duplicates('patient_id')

# Check for -999 in biomarker_baseline and exclude if present (though not needed for response rate)
# Since response rate depends only on 'responded', we don't need to filter on biomarker_baseline

# Verify the deduplication and data structure
print(f'Original rows: {len(df)}')
print(f'Unique patient_ids: {df["patient_id"].nunique()}')
print(f'Arm distribution: {df["arm"].value_counts()}')
print(f'Severity distribution: {df["severity"].value_counts()}')

# Stratify by severity and compute response rate difference (treatment - control)
severities = df["severity"].unique()
severities_list = list(severities)
severities_list.sort()

results = {}
for severity in severities_list:
    subset = df[df["severity"] == severity]
    treatment_rate = subset[subset["arm"] == "treatment"]["responded"].mean()
    control_rate = subset[subset["arm"] == "control"]["responded"].mean()
    diff = treatment_rate - control_rate
    results[severity] = diff

results"}
